```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(meddecide)
```

Every analysis in the jamovi module is also an R function with the same name.
The function arguments are the options of the jamovi panel; see the help page of
each function (for example `?decision`) for the full list.

## The 15 analyses

| Function | jamovi menu | Purpose | Article |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agreement()` | meddecide > Agreement > Interrater Reliability | Kappa, weighted kappa, ICC, Krippendorff's alpha, Gwet's AC1, Bland-Altman and related agreement statistics | [Agreement](03-agreement-analysis.html), [comprehensive](meddecide-agreement-comprehensive.html) |
| `decision()` | meddecide > Decision > Medical Decision | Sensitivity, specificity, predictive values and likelihood ratios from raw data against a reference standard | [Diagnostic tests](13-diagnostic-tests.html) |
| `decisioncombine()` | meddecide > Decision > Combine Medical Decision Tests | Accuracy of combinations (patterns) of up to three binary tests | |
| `decisioncompare()` | meddecide > Decision > Compare Medical Decision Tests | Compare the accuracy of up to three tests on the same patients | |
| `nogoldstandard()` | meddecide > Decision > Analysis Without Gold Standard | Latent models for 3-5 tests without a reference standard; reference-rule agreement for 2-5 tests | [No gold standard](12-nogoldstandard.html) |
| `decisioncalculator()` | meddecide > Decision Calculators > Medical Decision Calculator | Diagnostic accuracy from the four cell counts, with Fagan nomogram | [Diagnostic tests](13-diagnostic-tests.html) |
| `cotest()` | meddecide > Decision Calculators > Co-Testing Analysis | Post-test probabilities when two tests are done together, with or without conditional dependence | [Co-testing](34-cotest-analysis.html) |
| `sequentialtests()` | meddecide > Decision Calculators > Sequential Testing Analysis | Serial and parallel two-test strategies | [Sequential testing](36-sequential-testing-comprehensive.html) |
| `decisioncurve()` | meddecide > Decision Curve Analysis > Decision Curve Analysis | Net benefit of prediction models across threshold probabilities | |
| `enhancedROC()` | meddecide > ROC > Clinical ROC Analysis | ROC curves, AUC, optimal cut-offs and clinical metrics | [Clinical ROC](meddecide-enhancedroc-comprehensive.html) |
| `psychopdaROC()` | meddecide > ROC > Advanced ROC Analysis | ROC with many cut-point methods, DeLong comparison, IDI/NRI, decision curves | [ROC](03-roc-analysis.html), [comprehensive](meddecide-psychopdaroc-comprehensive.html) |
| `lassologistic()` | meddecide > Prediction Models > LASSO Logistic Regression | Penalised logistic regression for variable selection and risk scores | |
| `kappaSizeCI()` | Power > Power Analysis by meddecide > Confidence Interval Approach for the Number of Subjects Required | Sample size for a kappa confidence interval of a given width | [kappaSizeCI](07-kappasizeci-comprehensive.html) |
| `kappaSizePower()` | Power > Power Analysis by meddecide > Power Approach for the Number of Subjects Required | Sample size to test kappa against a null value | [kappaSizePower](09-kappasizepower-comprehensive.html) |
| `kappaSizeFixedN()` | Power > Power Analysis by meddecide > Lowest Expected Kappa for a Fixed Sample Size | Expected one-sided lower confidence bound at fixed N; not a power calculation | [kappaSizeFixedN](08-kappasizefixedn-comprehensive.html) |

## Calling conventions

- Pass columns **by name**: `gold = "gold"`, `vars = c("Rater1", "Rater2")`.
  A bare object name given to a variable argument is read as a column name, so
  build vectors of names inline (`vars = c(...)` or `vars = sprintf(...)`).
- Arguments of type *Level* (the positive and negative levels of an outcome or
  test, such as `goldPositive`/`goldNegative` in `decision()` or
  `positiveClass`/`negativeClass` in `psychopdaROC()`) have no default and must
  always be given. The analysis does not guess which level means "disease".
- The result is an object whose elements are the tables and plots of the jamovi
  output. Print it to see everything, or pick one element and convert a table
  with `$asDF`:

```{r example}
res <- decisioncalculator(TP = 90, FN = 10, TN = 80, FP = 20)
res$ratioTable$asDF
```

Some results sit inside groups and need a two-part path, for example
`agreement(...)$krippTableGroup$krippTable`.

For assumptions, denominator differences and validation status, see
[Choosing and interpreting an analysis](17-methods-and-interpretation.html).
